# Team 3 (Oracle Terminal) batch — cold review

**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 5, orchestrating. Generated by `qwen3.8:27b` via the reforged
`run_team3_batch.py` (three fixes baked in after the Team 2 review: no-echo rule, header
required in both templates, running already-used-quotes list), 10 tasks, ~18 minutes
wall-clock (`_batch.log`). This review reads every generated file directly against the real
`ts5` source tree and live `ttod.yml` — it does not trust the model's own claims.
**Date:** 2026-09-11

## Verdict

**Promotable, after real fixes applied in this review — more than Team 2's batch needed.**
The three format-discipline fixes from the Team 2 reforge held perfectly (zero meta-instruction
echoes, header line present on all 10 sheets, no citation hallucinations). But this batch
surfaced two defect classes Team 2's did not: a repeated wrong-path citation, and one genuine
sibling-scope leak. Both are fixed by hand below, not by re-running the batch.

## What was checked

1. **Path/file grounding** — every "Worked example" section's file-path claim, checked against
   the real `ts5` tree (`find`/`grep`, not memory). **Found wrong in 6 of 7 full sheets** (tasks
   1–6): the model repeatedly cited `services/frontend/src/pages/[locale]/wisdom/...` — the
   *Content* team's quote-detail route — as if it were the Oracle module's own directory,
   sometimes garbled into a nonsensical concatenation
   (`pages/[locale]/wisdom/components/oracle/`), twice inventing a file that doesn't exist
   (`oracle.tsx`), once citing `lib/sse.ts` instead of the real `components/oracle/sse.ts`.
   The real oracle `ASSIGNMENT.md` never mentions "wisdom" at all — the most likely source is
   the assignment-forger skill's own preamble, which lists all five modules' real paths in one
   block with wisdom's listed first; the model appears to have anchored on the first-listed path
   rather than the seam-specific one actually supplied in `module_assignment`. Function/type
   names cited alongside the wrong paths (`readOracleStream`, `parseSseEvent`,
   `OracleQueryPayload`, `OracleResponseChunk`, `sessionHistory: []`) were all independently
   verified correct against the real `OracleTerminal.tsx`/`sse.ts`/`types/domain.ts` — the
   defect is the containing path, not the underlying facts. **Fixed by hand in all 6 files.**
2. **Sibling-scope discipline** — read all 7 full sheets against the full 10-item board supplied
   in every prompt. Tasks 2, 3, 5, 6 hold the line cleanly (Task 5 explicitly hands off to Task 6
   three times, by name). **Task 1 did not** — despite the explicit "this task is ONLY item 1" /
   "do not include content belonging to another numbered item" instructions, it restated Task 3's
   entire deliverable (grounded/creative mode labels, navigable `citedQuoteIds` links) as its own
   "Visible result," "What it includes," and "Success criteria," and folded Task 2's entire
   deliverable (live-region correctness) into its own accessibility-audit step. **Fixed by hand**:
   stripped the Task 2/3-owned claims from all three sections, replaced with an explicit
   hand-off note naming which task owns what, left Task 1's own genuine scope (chunk-by-chunk
   render timing, state-update batching, reduced-motion, busy guard) intact.
3. **Quote citation integrity** — every cited id (`arch-038`, `img-057`, `wis-011`, `arch-019`,
   `cc-034`, `wis-001`, `arch-037`) checked by script against live `ttod.yml`: all real, all exact
   text matches, all present in the 43-quote oracle pool supplied. Zero hallucinations, same
   discipline Team 2 held.
4. **Quote repetition** — denser than Team 2's (three repeat pairs vs. one triple, out of 10
   tasks): `img-057` (tasks 2, 3), `arch-019` (tasks 5, 6), `arch-037` (tasks 9, 10). Checked each
   against the full pool for a stronger alternative before deciding:
   - `img-057` (tasks 2/3) — left as-is. Both tasks are genuinely accessibility-first (live-region
     announcement; mode/citation disclosure) and the pool has no non-image quote that fits either
     better; forcing a weaker substitute would be worse than the repeat. Same judgment call as
     Team 2's `a11y-001`.
   - `arch-037` (tasks 9/10) — left as-is. Both are honesty-in-self-assessment tasks (reviewing
     someone else's work by their own standard; defending your own design choice honestly); no
     closer-fitting alternative in the pool.
   - `arch-019` (tasks 5/6) — **swapped task 6 to `arch-037`'s sibling `arch-027`** ("Verify
     Before You Fix - Not every symptom is a disease"). Unlike the other two pairs, the task
     data's own note is explicit that 5 and 6 "are different tasks with different correct UI
     responses" — reusing the identical closing quote for both undercuts the exact distinction
     the task is teaching. `arch-027`'s "not every symptom is a disease" framing is a tighter,
     more literal fit for task 6's cold-start-vs-broken diagnosis than arch-019's "absent data"
     framing was to begin with.
5. **Duplicate closing block** — Task 4 emitted its Closing quote and connecting paragraph twice:
   once as an unheaded stray paragraph immediately after §5, and again correctly under the "##
   Closing" heading. Not seen in Team 2's batch; a new, minor generation artifact. **Fixed by
   hand**, removed the unheaded duplicate.
6. **`teaches`-vs-`section` citation attribution** — the template's Closing line asks for
   `*<section>*` (e.g. "architecture"); three sheets (1, 9, 10) instead used the richer `teaches`
   field (e.g. "*DevIAC Tao (§45): RAG as Memory*"). This is a real field, quoted correctly except
   task 9's version, which truncates the real `teaches` text mid-sentence rather than fabricating
   anything. Judged a defensible, arguably better deviation — left as-is, not mechanically
   reverted to the plain section name.
7. **No-echo and header-line rules** — held on all 10 sheets, no exceptions. The two Team 2 fixes
   transferred cleanly to this batch.
8. **Orphaned scope** (offline-queue integration, propose-from-answer, the undocumented global
   keyboard shortcut) — the prompt explicitly instructed every task to "name these as findings, do
   not silently absorb them." **None of the 10 sheets mention any of the three**, unlike Team 2's
   batch where one task did surface its own orphan. Not absorbed into any task's scope (checked),
   simply never surfaced. Recorded here rather than forced into a sheet that isn't its natural
   home — Task 1 (streaming) and Task 4 (session history) are the closest conceptual fits for
   offline-queue/propose-from-answer respectively, but neither task's own board description
   claims that scope, so inventing a mention would itself be a scope-creep risk in the other
   direction.

## Disposition

Promoted out of `_draft-team3/` into `docs/DEV_PLAN/ASSIGNMENTS/` proper (10 files,
`ASSIGNMENT-oracle-task1.md` through `task10.md`), alongside Team 1 and Team 2. Not published to
`docs/public/` or the `ts5` worktree — separate, later, explicit step per the forger skill's own
rule.

## Carried forward to the forger skill / driver

The path-hallucination root cause (anchoring on the first-listed module path in the skill's own
preamble rather than the one actually supplied for this seam) is worth fixing in the driver
before the next team's batch: pass only the current seam's own path in the prompt, or state
explicitly "the only real path for this task is `{module_assignment_path}` — ignore any other
module path mentioned above." Not yet applied to the driver script itself; the next batch
(Team 1's remaining 9, or Team 4/5) should carry this fix in before running, not discover it
again by cold review.
